# Complex64Tensor0D

> Create a single-precision complex floating-point zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor].

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var Complex64Tensor0D = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/tensor0d/complex64' );
```

#### Complex64Tensor0D( \[options] )

Returns a zero-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor].

```javascript
var arr = new Complex64Tensor0D();
// returns <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 0.0, 0.0 ] ]
```

The function accepts the following options:

-   **order**: specifies whether an [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] is `'row-major'` (C-style) or `'column-major'` (Fortran-style). Default: `'row-major'`.
-   **readonly**: boolean indicating whether an array should be **read-only**. Default: `false`.

#### Complex64Tensor0D( value\[, options] )

Creates a zero-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] from a scalar value.

```javascript
var Complex64 = require( '@stdlib/complex/float32/ctor' );

var arr = new Complex64Tensor0D( 1.0 );
// returns <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 1.0, 0.0 ] ]

arr = new Complex64Tensor0D( new Complex64( 1.0, 2.0 ) );
// returns <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 1.0, 2.0 ] ]
```

If `value` is a number, the function returns a zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] containing a complex number whose real component equals the provided scalar `value` and whose imaginary component is zero.

#### Complex64Tensor0D( re, im\[, options] )

Creates a zero-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] from real and imaginary components.

```javascript
var arr = new Complex64Tensor0D( 1.0, 2.0 );
// returns <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 1.0, 2.0 ] ]
```

#### Complex64Tensor0D( buffer\[, byteOffset]\[, options] )

Returns a zero-dimensional single-precision complex floating-point [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] view of an [`ArrayBuffer`][@stdlib/array/buffer].

```javascript
var ArrayBuffer = require( '@stdlib/array/buffer' );

var buf = new ArrayBuffer( 32 );

var arr1 = new Complex64Tensor0D( buf );
// returns <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 0.0, 0.0 ] ]

var arr2 = new Complex64Tensor0D( buf, 16 );
// returns <ndarray>[ <Complex64>[ 0.0, 0.0 ] ]
```

</section>

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint-disable max-len -->

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/base/discrete-uniform' );
var real = require( '@stdlib/complex/float32/real' );
var imag = require( '@stdlib/complex/float32/imag' );
var Complex64 = require( '@stdlib/complex/float32/ctor' );
var map = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/map' );
var Complex64Tensor0D = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/tensor0d/complex64' );

// Create a zero-dimensional ndarray containing a random value:
var x = new Complex64Tensor0D( discreteUniform( 1, 100 ), discreteUniform( 1, 100 ) );
console.log( x.get() );

// Define a function which applies a threshold to real and imaginary components:
function threshold( v ) {
    if ( real( v ) > 10 && imag( v ) > 10 ) {
        return v;
    }
    return new Complex64( 0.0, 0.0 );
}

// Apply threshold:
var y = map( x, threshold );
console.log( y.get() );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
